## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Gopālavimānavatthu* (Vv 80, translated as "Cow Herder’s Mansion") is a verse text belonging to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. In this narrative, a deva recounts how the compassion shown to him by the Arahant Moggallāna led to immense happiness and celestial reward.

 However, automated analysis by DharmaNexus documents extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 75 matching passages across 15 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The vast majority of these shared passages link directly to its commentary, the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (43 matches, including §1.1–4.2) [DharmaNexus]. Stock descriptions of celestial splendor are also shared with numerous other *Vimānavatthu* poems, most prominently *Anekavaṇṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 82, §3.3–6.1), *Cittalatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 75, §4.1–6.1), *Nandanavimānavatthu* (Vv 76, §4.1–6.1), and both *Kuṇḍalīvimānavatthu* texts (Vv 72 and Vv 73) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
